main_issue: How to get Agent D's half-done pitch section finished by Thursday after their grandmother's death: whether others take it on or D does it, and how teammates share the load.

A-B.evidence: B first said no capacity (14); after A's push for any help, B offered 'I can format the slides' (21) and A thanked B (22).

A-C.evidence: C refused to take the section (16) and the data help (23); after A offered a swap (25), C agreed: 'If you'll help me tomorrow morning, I can help with the data tonight' (26).

A-D.evidence: A urged D not to work tonight (18, 20) while D insisted 'I have to' (19); A then built a plan to ease it, thanked by D (27), though D still works tonight (28).

B-C.evidence: Both initially declined for lack of capacity (14, 16); B later helped with slides and C with data, but they never addressed each other.

B-D.evidence: B declined to take the section (14), then offered to format slides (21), supporting D's plan; no direct exchange between them.

C-D.evidence: C declined to help (23) and D said 'It's okay' (24); C later agreed to help with the data and D thanked C (26, 27).
